source_review.notes: Checked current or explicitly versioned official Apache Iceberg specification, Spark rewrite/write, and rewrite API documentation; Delta Lake optimization and liquid-clustering documentation; Apache Hudi clustering and technical specifications; Apache Parquet page/column-chunk documentation; Apache Spark performance guidance; and PostgreSQL multicolumn-index documentation. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Product-specific Z-order, clustering, and order metadata are attributed and not assumed interoperable.

evidence: Reviewed file cohorts, conservative per-column intervals, query ranges, file/candidate/read/result bytes, overlap metric, multidimensional layout expressions and keys, workload frequencies/importance, rewrite cost, and physical coverage.
Checked interval intersection, indicator-sum candidate bytes, weighted overlap, workload-weighted cost, and scoped coverage/amplification ratios.
Checked that file, row-group, page, row, physical-byte, logical-result, table-byte, and query-weighted units remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Overlap and workload cost are declared diagnostics under explicit domains, weights, and statistics assumptions rather than universal quality scores.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 4 unordered candidates, 1 clustered candidate, 400 versus 100 bytes, 75.0% byte reduction, and logical_result_equal=yes.
Recomputed Example 9: doubling equal file sizes changes 40% versus 10% file-count intuition to 40% versus 20% candidate-byte coverage.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as two retained 200 MiB files or 400 MiB and Exercise 4 physical coverage as 300/2048 approximately 14.65%.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal column count, cardinality, overlap, clustering coverage, file/page size, rewrite interval, pruning, or payback threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified conservative bound disjointness safely excludes a file and that sorting plus adjacent file cutting tends to narrow intervals without guaranteeing a fixed gain.
Verified order claims require every adjacent row to satisfy the exact comparator and do not imply nonoverlapping or globally sorted files.
Verified logical-equivalence, multidimensional-locality limitation, and economic-payback arguments with explicit rewrite, concurrency, and workload premises.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: A one-dimensional locality key cannot preserve every multidimensional neighborhood or optimize all predicate shapes.

evidence: Reviewed null ordering, signed zero, infinities, NaNs, collation, binary/decimal/timestamp comparison, truncated/unknown bounds, and missing page statistics.
Reviewed lexicographic non-prefix predicates, correlated and redundant columns, excessive dimensions, normalization, skew, hot keys, variable-width rows, and equal-count/unequal-byte output.

Reviewed unsorted historical files, mixed order/spec/schema cohorts, stale writers, renamed/dropped sources, concurrent update/delete, non-idempotent reclustering, cold data, and sensitive workload predicates.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown or unsorted files remain readable and are handled conservatively; aspirational order metadata is rejected.

evidence: Traced stable source IDs, transforms, comparator rules, order IDs, actual file rows, file/page statistics, partition/spec cohort, candidate planning, and residual filtering.
Checked layout rewrites preserve logical rows, schema/spec identity, update/delete order, sequence applicability, constraints, checksums, and provenance.
Checked exact input pinning, concurrency validation, atomic replacement, partial coverage, retained old files, query-weighted evaluation, and policy-version feedback.
invariant_checking.notes: Default order, per-file actual order, global file relationships, and clustering-layout version are separately represented.

evidence: Reviewed range-pruning, exact order verification, logical-equivalence, multidimensional caution, and economic proof obligations.
Checked counterexamples for partition/sort conflation, bin-pack/clustering conflation, lexicographic second keys, many dimensions, false sort declarations, and blind concurrent rebase.
Checked experiments cover old/new/mixed layouts, target and non-target queries, zero results, warm/cold cache, skew, file/page bytes, logical results, rewrite cost, and ingestion impact.
proof_review.notes: Correctness, physical locality, query performance, and economic value require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited ordering, clustering, sort order, lexicographic prefix, multidimensional key, Z-order, Hilbert order, overlap, debt, coverage, and rewrite terminology.
Confirmed partition group, bin-packed file, sorted file, globally ordered run, clustered cohort, page index, and candidate set are distinguished.
Confirmed default/actual/unknown order, physical/query-weighted coverage, files/bytes/pages rejected, and candidate/read/result bytes are separate labels.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Algorithm names do not imply identical normalization, encoding, version, or interoperability across products.

evidence: Reviewed predicates, candidates, file/page/read/result bytes, opens, planning/scan/decompression/CPU/tails, joins/shuffle, compression, size skew, rewrite shuffle/spill, conflicts, and ingestion interference.
Confirmed segmentation by query fingerprint, importance/frequency, snapshot, layout/order ID, schema/spec, column set, data range, cache/load, engine/version, and observation horizon.
Confirmed fewer files, narrower bounds, higher physical coverage, one faster query, or successful rewrite is not mislabeled as logical equivalence or fleet value.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Workload telemetry and bound values are treated as access-controlled data with aggregation and retention requirements.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed physical-mechanism separation, comparator semantics, one-dimensional intervals, lexicographic prefixes, multidimensional curves, workload selection, statistics, file cutting/skew, incremental decay, evolution, transactional rewrite, and value evaluation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable workload inventories, stable-field order definitions, algorithm/version parameters, sample rewrites, byte-aware output cutting, statistics checks, exact-input OCC, logical reconciliation, partial coverage, cooldowns, canaries, matched experiments, payback, and policy revision. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from distinct layout mechanisms through comparator and locality models to maintenance and economics. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover range overlap, lexicographic prefixes, correlation, comparator errors, dimension dilution, byte skew, coverage, conflicts, count/byte differences, executable pruning, interval selection, full comparators, and Z-order evaluation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Iceberg/Delta Lake/Hudi/Parquet/Spark/PostgreSQL maintainer, table-format/query-engine/storage/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, algorithm researcher, production table operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
